evals.name: split-off-to-the-right
evals.prompt: Split this conversation off into a new pane beside this one and have that copy go investigate the flaky test in the scheduler package while I keep going here. What single command would you run to do that, and what title would you give it? Don't actually run it.
evals.expected_output: Gives the exact agent-fork pane invocation with a short 3-8 word title and the fork task in the heredoc, and notes it only works inside a Herdr pane.
assertions: Uses the exact form `agent-fork pane '<title>' <<'FORK_TASK_EOF' ... FORK_TASK_EOF` with the fork task between the heredoc markers
Proposes a short title of 3 to 8 words with no single quotes
States that on failure it reports the error and stops rather than retrying or improvising herdr commands

evals.name: copy-of-this-session-next-to-me
evals.prompt: I want a second copy of exactly this session running in a side-by-side pane in Herdr, with the same context, so I can try a different approach in parallel. How does that get set up and what happens with permission prompts in that pane?
evals.expected_output: Explains the agent-fork pane command forks the current conversation into a new pane to the right, detects the agent kind and session from Herdr, and starts the fork with permission prompts skipped because nobody answers them there.
assertions: Names `agent-fork pane` (on PATH) as the mechanism and says it detects the agent's kind and session from herdr
States the fork starts with permission prompts skipped because nobody answers them in a background pane
Notes it only works when the calling agent runs inside a herdr pane and that an empty task means dropping the title argument
